items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: In my case it was the people like Benny Goodman and Roy Eldridge and Maxine Sullivan and Vic Dickinson and Scott Hamilton and Ruby Braff, and Kenny Davern and Bob Wilber and those kind of people

ctx.x: How long did you stay in New York and did you get out doing road work with those particular — with Scott, you did some traveling?

Well I got out with Scott quite a bit. I think we didn’t work as much as a lot of people thought we did. I remember I think it was 1978, we’d been there a year and a half or so, where we had our best year on the road, I think we did 14 weeks on the road. And we never did as much as that again. Although we did anywhere from half to two thirds of that or something, for the next almost ten years. But everyone was relying more and more on freelancing in the New York area, and picking up whatever you could on the road…
What was it like to play behind Benny Goodman?
